title: Turmeric (Haldi) wound-healing patent revocation — US Patent 5,401,504
forum_or_authority: United States Patent and Trademark Office (re-examination), on CSIR challenge
citation_ref: US Patent 5,401,504 (granted 1995 to University of Mississippi; all claims cancelled on re-examination, 1997)
holding_or_summary: A US product patent claiming the use of turmeric powder for wound healing was revoked after India's CSIR filed re-examination evidence (including ancient Sanskrit texts and a paper in the Journal of the Indian Medical Association) proving the use was traditional knowledge and lacked novelty. The case is the founding precedent for TKDL as defensive prior art.

title: Neem fungicide patent revocation — EP 0436257
forum_or_authority: European Patent Office (Opposition Division; confirmed by Technical Board of Appeal)
citation_ref: EP 0436257 (W.R. Grace; revoked in opposition proceedings, appeal dismissed T 0416/01, 2005)
holding_or_summary: A European patent on a neem-oil fungicidal formulation was revoked after oppositions (including by the Government of India) demonstrated prior traditional use of neem extracts in India. The EPO held the claimed invention lacked novelty and inventive step over documented traditional knowledge.

title: Novartis AG v. Union of India — Section 3(d) enhanced-efficacy standard
citation_ref: Novartis AG v. Union of India (2013) 6 SCC 1
holding_or_summary: The Supreme Court upheld the rejection of a patent for the beta-crystalline form of imatinib mesylate, holding that under Section 3(d) of the Patents Act, 1970 a new form of a known substance is patentable only if it demonstrates significantly enhanced therapeutic efficacy, proved with clear research data. This is the controlling standard for any derivative / new-form Ayurvedic claim.
source_label: Supreme Court of India — official website (search neutral citation (2013) 6 SCC 1)

title: CGPDTM examination practice for TK-related patent applications
forum_or_authority: Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks — Manual of Patent Office Practice and Procedure
citation_ref: Manual of Patent Office Practice and Procedure (CGPDTM), chapters on non-patentable subject matter and TKDL prior-art search
holding_or_summary: Indian examiners must object to claims that aggregate traditionally known properties of Ayurvedic components (Sections 3(p)/3(e)), consult TKDL/AFI prior art during search, and require synergy/efficacy data before withdrawing the objection. Process claims with novel parameters are examined on their own merits.
source_label: IP India (CGPDTM) — Manual of Patent Office Practice and Procedure

title: NBA prior-approval procedure for IPR based on Indian biological resources
forum_or_authority: National Biodiversity Authority — Biological Diversity Rules (Form III procedure)
citation_ref: Biological Diversity Act, 2002 s.6(1) read with Biological Diversity Rules — Form III application to NBA before IPR filing
holding_or_summary: Any person applying for intellectual property rights in or outside India for an invention based on research or information on a biological resource obtained from India must obtain prior NBA approval (Form III) before filing. Benefit-sharing terms may be imposed; foreign filings additionally engage Section 3 (Form I).
source_label: National Biodiversity Authority — official portal (Form III procedure)

title: AYUSH licensing for patent & proprietary Ayurvedic medicines (Rule 158B / Schedule T)
forum_or_authority: Ministry of Ayush — Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945
citation_ref: Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, Rule 158B and Schedule T (GMP for ASU drugs)
holding_or_summary: Manufacture of patent or proprietary Ayurvedic medicines requires a State Licensing Authority licence supported by pilot safety/efficacy evidence beyond classical formulations, plus Schedule T Good Manufacturing Practices. This is the commercialisation path where product patenting is barred.
source_label: Ministry of Ayush — official portal (ASU drug licensing)

title: Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) as defensive prior-art system
forum_or_authority: Council of Scientific & Industrial Research (CSIR) with Department of AYUSH
citation_ref: TKDL database — codified formulations transcribed in IPC-compatible format and shared with international patent offices under access agreements
holding_or_summary: TKDL converts classical Ayurvedic/Unani/Siddha formulations into structured, searchable prior art in international patent-classification format. Under WIPO GRATK Article 4, such information systems are formally integrated into international examination, so TKDL-cited formulations can defeat novelty worldwide.
